data.body: RCA/design note: the defect is host-level aggregate resource use, not an individual failing test. I chose candidate (c), minimal both: a portable Makefile-side Python runner registers active full-suite runs in the git common dir, prunes stale pid records, and computes an effective xdist worker count from requested workers, available RAM (4 GiB/worker budget), CPU count, and active full-suite run count. It does not globally serialize development: multiple suites can still run, but each degrades its worker count; low-memory kills remain classified as environmental with serial fallback guidance. I rejected a pure semaphore because it risks queueing/starving agents or serializing full suites outright, and rejected memory-only autoscaling because simultaneous starts can all observe the same free-memory snapshot.
